items.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
items.detail: UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability that allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. Catalog addition date is not the attack date.

items.title: CVE-2026-123039: Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability
items.detail: Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). items.title: Momentum Telecom By endzone
items.detail: Momentum is a telecommunications company founded in 2001 that provides cloud-based communication solutions for businesses, specializing in cloud voice services, managed networks, SD-WAN solutions, and Microsoft Teams Phone integration. We gained access to a diagnostic and provisioning tool used by Momentum through a compromised Multi-Service Operator (MSO). Upon reconnaissance, we identified multiple critical vulnerabilities throughout the system. This tool controls internet and voice services for millions of users across global markets. We successfully accessed user data for every MSO, exposing personally identifiable information (PII) for over 7.5 million users. They didn't notice the prolonged access or the customer data dump for a while, but when we started deleting modems they noticed. They kept burning access and we gained it back, they'd burn it again. We have caused widespread outages (https://www.abc4.com/news/wasatch-front/eagle-mountain-internet-outage-cyberattack/). We now have had over 100,000 packages successfully deleted. That's 100,000+ people without internet service right now. Families, businesses, students all cut off from the digital world. This is the direct result of their negligence and failure to secure their systems. These services can be restored immediately with the click of a button on our tool but you must reach out. Click "View Affected MSOs" below to see the full list of compromised providers. Momentum management should contact us to discuss resolution. Affected MSOs can also contact us to have their users' data deleted from our database. Ransomware group claim; not independently verified. The observation/publication date is not the attack date.
